title: Inside kiln, Option/Ctrl+arrow arrive as plain arrows in iTerm2, so word motion moves one character
observed: kiln pushes the kitty keyboard protocol (CSI > 1 u, seen in a TEA_TRACE of kiln's output). Probed with a raw byte logger in iTerm2's Default profile via Orca: without that mode Option+Left = ESC[1;3D, Ctrl+Left = ESC[1;5D; with CSI > 1 u set, both arrive as plain ESC[D, so kiln's alt+left word motion moves one character ('hello worlNEWd'). With the mode set, Shift+Enter = ESC[13;2u (distinguishable, which the mode is for) and Option+Backspace = ESC[127u.
expected: Word motion by Option/Ctrl+arrow works inside kiln in iTerm2's Default profile. Caveat: the modifier loss was observed with Orca's synthetic key events; it needs confirming with a physical keypress before choosing between dropping kitty mode (losing Shift+Enter) and another route.

fix.note: Not a kiln bug: Andre confirmed on 2026-09-27 that a physical Option+Left in kiln's prompt in iTerm2 moves by a word. The modifier loss happens only with Orca's synthetic key events under the kitty keyboard protocol, so input/word-motion's alt+arrow steps cannot be driven through Orca.
